text:
nina-sec: Heads up team — security advisory and required action: we found a stale CI cache that contained long-lived service API keys for a handful of internal service accounts. No evidence of external exfil, but this is high risk. Were moving to immediate revocation + mandatory OIDC short-lived tokens for all service accounts.

raj-infra: Where were the keys stored? Which projects affected?

nina-sec: Keys appeared in `ci/cache/artifacts` for two repos: infra-templates and notifications. Affected service accounts: `svc-notify-prod`, `svc-telemetry-ingest`. CI runs that reused the cache in the last 60 days may have seen the keys.

ci-bot: Alert generated: https://ci.redwood-internal/jobs/alerts/ALERT-6123. I scanned runs with cache:false and found 23 runs that cached artifacts containing `api_key=`.

marta-cs: Any customer impact?

nina-sec: None known for external customers. These are internal service accounts used to push metrics and send operational alerts. Still, we must treat as high priority.

oliver-legal: For compliance, we need an internal incident log, who had access, and the rotation evidence. Also notify Data Privacy for telemetry data scope.

raj-infra: Immediate remediation plan: 1) Revoke the two exposed keys now, 2) Issue short-lived OIDC tokens for the affected service accounts, 3) Add CI job step to purge caches and rotate any keys found, 4) Enforce repo pre-commit hook to block committed secrets.

nina-sec: Agreed. Timeline: revoke keys now (T+30m), patch CI pipelines and enable token exchange (T+4h), org-wide migration deadline (T+7 days) to OIDC. After 7 days any remaining long-lived keys will be revoked.

raj-infra: Commands to rotate and revoke (internal tools):

raj-infra: ```bash
# revoke current key
redwood-cli iam revoke-key --service-account svc-notify-prod --key-id 0xA3B4C
# create OIDC role binding
redwood-cli iam create-oidc-binding --sa svc-notify-prod --audience ci-runner --ttl 3600
```

tyler-eng: For teams, what's the easiest migration path? Example snippet for github actions and our OIDC token exchange?

raj-infra: Example (GH Actions):

raj-infra: ```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Request OIDC token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(curl -s -H "Metadata: true" "https://oauth.redwood-internal/token?aud=ci-runner&sa=svc-notify-prod")
          export REDWOOD_TOKEN="$TOKEN"
      - name: Use token
        run: ./deploy.sh --token "$REDWOOD_TOKEN"
```

nina-sec: We'll publish a migration guide with templates for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins. Link will go to https://wiki.redwood-internal/security/oidc-migration (drafting).

marta-cs: I'll prepare a short internal email to dev teams linking the guide and explaining the 7-day deadline. Also offer remediation assistance for critical services.

oliver-legal: Include language about audit logs and the fact we will revoke keys after the deadline. Also provide contact for escalation if a team cannot migrate in time due to third-party constraints.

ci-bot: I've queued a CI sweep job to purge caches containing `api_key=` and create a ticket per repo with findings. Ticket: SEC-6123.

raj-infra: Add guardrails: 1) repo policy to block commits with `api_key` pattern, 2) CI will fail if cache contains base64 blobs >1MB without whitelabel, 3) enable secret scanning alerts in repo settings.

nina-sec: Action owners: Raj (infra) implements token exchange + guardrails; Tyler & Eng leads coordinate migration for app teams; Marta handles comms; Legal handles compliance copy.

tyler-eng: Noted. I'll add the migration task to our sprint and start migrating the notifications service this afternoon.

nina-sec: Follow-up: after revocation and migration, we'll run an audit of outbound connections from the affected services to verify no anomalous endpoints were contacted. We'll file a short incident summary within 3 business days.

marta-cs: Sending draft email now. Will post back with CS and workspace channels copy.

oliver-legal: Also request retention of the CI logs for 90 days for the investigation.

nina-sec: Thanks all. If you find any other long-lived keys during the sweep, tag SEC-6123 and escalate immediately. :lock:
